speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) since the implementation of the private hire driver's vocational licence, what has been the passing rate for applicants; and (b) whether the Ministry will consider allowing the tests to be conducted in vernacular languages, especially for older drivers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: This is so that they can navigate roads and buildings, the names of which are primarily in English.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Two supplementary questions: the first is, because at base, ride-hailing is fairly straightforward with locations clearly marked out.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Is there then scope for us to have a simplified version of tests, especially for those with language difficulties?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: And second, for those who have engaged in longer-term contracts with the ride-hire companies to rent the vehicles, can there be an extension for them in order to pass the test in time?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: To the first point, ride-hailing, when it goes as intended, is a simple process.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But the regulation of this space has to take into account what happens when things go wrong, when accidents occur, when other things occur on the roads, pedestrians and so forth.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, when things go wrong, there is a need to interface with members of the public, members of the emergency services, rescue services and security services.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I take the point that ride-hailing, when it works well and works as designed, it is a simple process, but it operates in a fairly complicated environment, and how we regulate all the users of that environment will have to take all of that into account.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: If there are specific cases that the Member is interested in, he can perhaps write to me and I could follow up on how we might assist these drivers.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Can I just ask the Senior Minister of State would the Ministry consider allowing tests to be conducted for persons with hearing disabilities?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: If the Member has specific instances of drivers who would like to apply, maybe he can write to me and I could follow up on that.
